children: CoreWeave stock CRWV declined 6% on Monday as technology stocks continued to fall on Monday. Nvidia's fall also affected CoreWeave's decline, as Nvidia holds stakes in the neo cloud company.
Fellow neo cloud company Nebius also fell 6.7% in the session after analysts cut the target price on the stock.
CoreWeave shares have come under pressure throughout 2026, falling almost 30% amid concerns about the company's debt levels and substantial capital spending requirements.
However, Nvidia's leadership transition has added another layer of uncertainty for investors, given the chipmaker's financial and strategic relationship with CoreWeave.
Nvidia leadership uncertainty raises concerns for CoreWeave
Nvidia's leadership shock has emerged as a key factor weighing on sentiment towards CoreWeave.
The decline comes days after Nvidia announced the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang and began searching for his successor.
Huang's departure has raised questions about Nvidia's future hardware roadmap and its financing commitments to companies that rely heavily on its GPUs.
CoreWeave's AI cloud business is particularly exposed to these developments because of its dependence on Nvidia hardware.
Investors are also assessing the potential implications of tighter US restrictions on advanced chip exports to China.
Nvidia is expected to report revenue of $109.08 billion and earnings per share of $2.48.
The upcoming results have become an important event for investors as they assess the company's growth outlook following Huang's departure.
Concerns about a potential pullback in Nvidia's investments and expansion plans could also create financing challenges for AI cloud providers such as CoreWeave.
Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges lowered her price target on CoreWeave to $101 from $106 but maintained a Buy rating on the shares.
"We remain Buy rated and adjust our 12-month price target to $101 (from $106) based on 15x EV/EBIT to CoreWeave's SNTM non-GAAP EBIT," the Goldman Sachs analyst said.
Nvidia's financial and commercial ties with CoreWeave
Nvidia has established a significant financial and strategic position in CoreWeave through a series of investments.
The chipmaker first invested in CoreWeave during its 2023 Series B funding round.
It held approximately 6% of the company when CoreWeave went public in 2025.
Nvidia subsequently invested another $2 billion in January 2026, increasing its stake to approximately 9%.
Nvidia had committed more than $40 billion to AI investments in 2026, with Huang playing an active role in those deals.
The relationship extends beyond equity investments.
Nvidia has also committed to purchasing CoreWeave's unsold cloud-computing capacity under a multi-year agreement.
The agreement involves at least $6.3 billion in purchases through April 2032.
These commitments have helped support CoreWeave's business model, but they also highlight the company's dependence on Nvidia's financial and commercial support.
Huang previously defended CoreWeave's financing position
Huang had publicly defended CoreWeave's financial position during its October stock and bond selloff.
At the time, he said CoreWeave did not need "a backstop or a bailout" and argued that its "cost of capital is actually decreasing."
His comments sought to address concerns that CoreWeave's high borrowing costs could eventually force Nvidia to provide additional financial support.
However, Huang's departure has raised questions about whether the same level of strategic and financial support will continue under Nvidia's future leadership.
For CoreWeave investors, the key issues remain the company's ability to finance its substantial infrastructure expansion, manage its debt and maintain access to Nvidia's GPUs.
